[[File:KOCIS Royal Azalea (8573227639).jpg|thumb|Flowers]]

'''''Rhododendron schlippenbachii''''', the '''royal azalea''', is a species of ''[[Rhododendron]]'' native to the [[Korean Peninsula]] and adjacent regions of [[Northeast China]], [[Japan]], and the [[Russian Far East]]. It is the dominant understory shrub in many Korean hillside forests, growing at {{convert|400-1500|m|ft|abbr=on}} altitude.

==Description==
It is a dense [[deciduous]] [[shrub]] growing to {{convert|4.5|m|ft|abbr=on}} in height, but more commonly {{convert|1-2|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall. The [[leaf|leaves]] are obovate, {{convert|4.5|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|2.5-4.5|cm|in|abbr=on}} broad, with scattered [[Glandular hair|glandular hairs]]. The [[flower]]s are white to pink, often with small red spots on the upper three petals; they are produced in late spring to early summer.

The scientific name ''schlippenbachii'' is derived from [[Baron von Schlippenbach]], a Russian officer who collected the species in 1854.

==Cultivation and symbolism==
In Korean language, it is called {{Langx|ko|철쭉|translit=cheoljjuk|label=none}} and if the color of the petals is white, the flower is called {{Langx|ko|흰철쭉|translit=huincheoljjuk|label=none}}.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.seongju.go.kr/english/culture/plant3_24.jsp |title=Welcome to SeongJu County |access-date=2008-06-28 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20071020013417/http://www.seongju.go.kr/english/culture/plant3_24.jsp |archive-date=2007-10-20 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aku.or.kr/cgi/read.cgi?board=02_1_2_4&y_number=108&nnew=2 |script-title=ko:철쭉 |trans-title=Azaleas |publisher=Anyang Kunfo Uwang Federation for Environmental Movement Association |language=Korean |access-date=2008-06-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722140747/http://www.aku.or.kr/cgi/read.cgi?board=02_1_2_4&y_number=108&nnew=2 |archive-date=2011-07-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The Royal Azalea is commonly chosen as a local symbol in [[South Korea]], by provinces, cities and counties such as [[Gangwon Province (South Korea)|Gangwon Province]], [[Gapyeong]] and [[Miryang]].

It is widely cultivated in many parts of the world; some [[cultivar]]s bear white flowers. The fruit is egg-shaped and oval, {{convert|1.5|cm|in|abbr=on}} long, with glandular hair, which ripen in October. Azaleas are poisonous and can not be eaten.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://terms.naver.com/entry.nhn?docId=1146423&cid=40942&categoryId=32723 |title=Rhododendron schlippenbachii |last= |first= |date= |website=terms.naver.com |access-date=}}{{dead link|date=June 2018|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>
